Definition: from G260; properly, to collect, i.e. (by implication) reap:--reap down.
BiblicalUsage: Once, and it is the cry of the unpaid: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth. The word is to reap, to gather the harvest, and the wages of the reapers are the charge against the rich.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for reaping carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the cry with it, that the hire kept back by fraud is heard in heaven even when the labourers are not.
